name: 46,XX Difference of Sex Development Induced by Endogenous Maternal-Derived Androgen

criteria.description: Presence of 46,XX karyotype without Y chromosome material
Evidence or history of elevated endogenous maternal androgen levels during pregnancy
Clinical signs of virilization such as clitoromegaly or labioscrotal fusion in the neonate
Presence of normal internal female reproductive structures (uterus, ovaries) confirmed by imaging or surgery
Exclusion of other causes of 46,XX DSD such as congenital adrenal hyperplasia or androgen-secreting tumors

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of 46,XX karyotype, documented maternal endogenous androgen excess during pregnancy, and clinical virilization of external genitalia in the neonate
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on clinical history and exclusion of other etiologies.

pathognomonic.notes: Enlargement of the clitoris due to androgen exposure
Partial or complete fusion of the labia resembling scrotum
Presence of uterus and ovaries despite external virilization

common.notes: Narrowing or underdevelopment of the vaginal canal
Increased terminal hair growth in androgen-sensitive areas
Genital appearance not clearly male or female

common.symptomName: Normal female gonadal function at birth
common.notes: Ovarian hormone production consistent with female phenotype
searchTerms: normal female gonad function at birth

occasional.notes: Greater than typical distance between anus and genitalia
searchTerms: longer distance between anus and genitals

occasional.notes: Changes in tactile sensitivity of the clitoris
Temporary adrenal enzyme activity changes mimicking CAH
searchTerms: short-term adrenal hormone excess in newborn

occasional.notes: Acne-like skin lesions due to androgen effect

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric distress related to ambiguous genitalia
rare.notes: Emotional or psychological impact in early childhood
searchTerms: psychological issues due to ambiguous genitals
emotional problems related to genital ambiguity

rare.notes: Elevated blood pressure possibly linked to hormonal imbalance
searchTerms: high blood pressure from androgen excess
raised blood pressure due to androgens

rare.notes: Development of cysts in ovarian tissue

laboratory: Elevated maternal serum androgen levels during pregnancy
Normal neonatal serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone and cortisol levels
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound showing normal uterus and ovaries
MRI confirming absence of testicular tissue
genetic: Absence of SRY gene or Y chromosome material
No mutations in CYP21A2 or other adrenal enzyme genes
other: Maternal history of conditions causing endogenous androgen excess (e.g., luteoma, hyperreactio luteinalis)

redFlags: Severe virilization of external genitalia in a 46,XX neonate
Maternal signs of androgen excess during pregnancy
Absence of adrenal enzyme abnormalities despite virilization
